rationale.complete: Round 1 done: calibrated synthetic battery at three real schedules (7 conditions, 630 replicates), 46 replication units (23 regime III, 23 regime I), four native tests (NE43, #44, #51, NE14), per-period verdicts, scorecard; everything rebuilt after the activity-bins join bug; confirmatory script frozen and dry-run, holdout not run.
rationale.faithfulness: The core prediction failed: the trimmed regime-III excess is not concentrated in a few pairs (P2 0/10), individual bonds are at the false floor and don't replicate (r 0.02), the known #44 team is not a bond cluster, and the dense rival is favored. What held (bonds below percolation, trimming removes bonds in III) is trivial or inherited from H38. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G0 H0 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A clear operator-level negative with a computable check: after schedule trimming, test whether co-activation is concentrated (CV-C10, split-half bond reliability) before targeting pairs; here it is a swarm-wide mode. Plus a calibrated pairwise-bond pipeline and the corrected NE43 date. It does not give a lever.

one_line: After the daily schedule is trimmed, regime-III co-activation is a weak swarm-wide mode, not small coupled clusters; bonds sit at the false-positive floor.

models.note: Dilute bond clusters refuted; excess is a dense swarm-wide mode

v2.claim: Edge-trimmed regime-III excess is a dense/shared-field mode, not a dilute ferromagnet
v2.rater: 2 raters (coordinator + blind); log-odds mean credence, mean V

raters.claim: Scope: 23 regime-III and 23 regime-I units, equal-time activity bonds after edge trimming. Trimmed regime-III co-activation is a weak structureless common mode, not a dilute set of strong pair bonds: 38 bonds vs ~23 expected false; the top 10% of pairs carry a median 11% of the excess (0/10 units concentrated); bonds do not recur.

replication: 0/10 units with excess are concentrated
robust: rebuilt after the activity-bins bug, no verdict change
